title: Hearing ragtime and jazz piano in Beardstown
summary: He knew syncopation from the start through a piano-playing friend of his father's and the improvising theater pianist Leo Boylen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, when did you -- when did you first start playing syncopation?
-- I knew what that was. I knew that before I started playing. I was interested in that, cause a fella that worked with my father was a great piano player, I mean jazz piano player.
Yeah, he even had a music store in town and I used to go by and he used to play oh, play blues and all these ragtime pieces and --
And the piano player in the theater used to play wonderful ragtime playing, just improvising ragtime.
Was the piano player you were talking about --
Yeah, Leo Boylen, yeah he was wonderful at that, improvising, --
-- cause he'd improvise all those things for the cartoon comedies --
-- he was very adept at it. And I used to ask him how he does it, you know?
-- he just say, well I don't know I just -- just --
He had wonderful hands, and then this piano player used to play slow things, like slow blues and thing, just improvising.
